entities.name: Publius Ostorius Scapula
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Ostorius Scapula was a Roman governor and general who ruled Britain from 47 CE until his death in 52 CE. He played a crucial role in the pacification of the island following the rebellion of the native Celtic leader, Caratacus.

As governor, Scapula oversaw the construction of roads, bridges, and public buildings, which helped to integrate the Roman province into the wider Roman Empire. He also promoted trade and commerce, establishing Britain as a major hub for Roman merchants.

Scapula's legacy extends beyond his military campaigns, as he helped to establish a more stable and prosperous Roman Britain. His reign marked the beginning of a period of relative peace and prosperity in the region, which would last for centuries.

In the centuries following his death, Scapula was remembered as a skilled and effective administrator who had brought order and stability to the turbulent region of Britain.

The Roman historian Tacitus wrote of Scapula's achievements in his work 'The Histories', noting that he was a 'most excellent governor' who had brought 'great prosperity and security' to Britain.
